proposal: The Mandate recommends eliminating SEC administrative proceedings other than stop orders on defective registration statements, since the enforcement system does not need both district court cases and proceedings. As an alternative it would let respondents elect an administrative forum or an ordinary Article III federal court.
remaining: Rule or statute ending administrative proceedings or giving respondents an election

status_summary: No SEC rule, statement or enacted law eliminating administrative proceedings or creating a respondent election was found. Press reporting dated 2025-05 says the SEC filed several contested fraud actions in federal court in April 2025, consistent with the 2024-06-27 Supreme Court decision in SEC v. Jarkesy, but that reporting does not say administrative proceedings were discontinued. No 119th Congress bill on this subject was identified in the searches run.
title: Eliminate SEC administrative proceedings or let respondents elect a federal court
uncertainties: No SEC rule, statement or enacted law eliminating administrative proceedings or creating a respondent election was found. SEC final rules since 2025 that touch the Rules of Practice concern stays of staff decisions and delegations. H.R. 9329, reported 2026-09-03, changes penalty counting and does not end administrative proceedings; its bill status file was not fetched. Reporting of April 2025 federal court filings after SEC v. Jarkesy does not say proceedings were discontinued, and the D&O Diary date is approximate. The SEC Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026', 38 rules) lists no rulemaking on administrative proceedings or forum. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
